title: New York's 1st Congressional District election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for New York's 1st Congressional District will determine who represents the eastern end and North Shore of Long Island, including the Hamptons, Riverhead, Smithtown, and Shelter Island in Suffolk County. Incumbent Republican Rep. Nick LaLota, first elected in 2022 and re-elected in 2024 with 55.5% of the vote, is seeking a third term. Two Democrats, Chris Gallant and Lukas Ventouras, are competing in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary for the chance to challenge LaLota in a district that Cook Political Report rates as Solid Republican. The race will test whether Democratic messaging on affordability and health care can overcome the district's recent Republican lean, with independent candidates also filing to run.

polling.pollster: Public Policy Polling (D) for House Majority PAC

polling_note: Only one publicly available poll was found. It was conducted by a Democratic-leaning organization (House Majority PAC) and shows a close race between LaLota and Gallant, with 20% undecided. The general election is still months away and the Democratic nominee has not yet been determined.

candidates.name: Nick LaLota
candidates.summary: Nick LaLota is the incumbent U.S. Representative for New York's 1st Congressional District, first elected in 2022 and re-elected in 2024. A Navy veteran and former Suffolk County Board of Elections commissioner, he serves on the House Appropriations Committee and is a member of the moderate Republican Governance Group and Problem Solvers Caucus. LaLota is running for a third term emphasizing his record on fiscal responsibility, supporting law enforcement, and protecting Long Island's coastal communities.

candidates.name: Chris Gallant
candidates.summary: Chris Gallant is a U.S. Army veteran, Black Hawk helicopter pilot, FAA air traffic controller, union leader, and volunteer firefighter running for Congress in New York's 1st District. He has been endorsed by former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg, former Congressman John Avlon, and the New York Working Families Party. Gallant's campaign focuses on affordability for Long Island families, protecting Medicare and Medicaid, coastal resilience, and accountable government.

candidates.summary: Lukas Ventouras is a first-generation American attorney and law student running for Congress in New York's 1st District. A graduate of NYU and a student at St. John's University School of Law, he previously interned for Congresswoman Grace Meng and served as president of the NYU chapter of Students Demand Action. Ventouras is campaigning on a platform of ending corruption, protecting reproductive freedom, expanding healthcare access, and addressing climate change.

forecast.rationale: Incumbent Rep. Nick LaLota (R) is seeking a third term in a district Cook Political Report rates as Solid Republican. He won re-election in 2024 with 55.5% of the vote, a clear but not overwhelming margin. The only available poll is a single nonpartisan-grade survey from December 2025 commissioned by a Democratic-aligned group (House Majority PAC), showing LaLota ahead of Democrat Chris Gallant 41%-38% with 20% undecided — suggesting potential competitiveness but with notable caveats: the poll is 6 months old, sponsor-aligned, and taken before the Democratic nominee was determined. The Democratic primary (June 23, 2026) is still 3 days away, with two candidates (Chris Gallant and Lukas Ventouras) competing; the eventual nominee's strength is unknown. With only 1 poll from a partisan source, a large undecided share, and an unsettled general election field, there is meaningful uncertainty. However, LaLota's incumbency, his 55.5% performance in 2024, the district's Republican lean in recent cycles, and the Cook rating all point to a clear Republican advantage — enough for a 'likely_r' rating (roughly 80-94% range) rather than safe_r, but not narrow enough for a tossup or lean given available evidence.
